Do you hate me?” he asked, a tremor in his voice betraying his bravado. His armor of cruelty cracked just enough for her to glimpse the man beneath.
“I do not hate you, Darren,” she replied softly, stepping closer, unafraid. “But I pity you—trapped as you are in all this darkness.”
In that moment, something shifted. His green eyes searched hers, the conflict of emotions playing across his handsome features as desire battled with the remnants of his humanity.
Her courage ignited a spark within him. “Perhaps I have kept you here too long,” he mused, his voice low, filled with a haunting vulnerability. “Perhaps it is I who is indeed the captive, wrestling with the ghosts of my past.”
As she reached out to touch his cheek, he flinched at first, but then leaned into her hand, allowing the warmth of her touch to seep into his guarded heart. 
His eyes were a peculiar feature, changing color depending on his mood. When he was feeling greedy, mean, possessive, or jealous, they would flash a deep shade of green. When he was kind, empathetic, or closer to human emotions (a rare occurrence), they would turn a warm green hazel. But most of the time, his eyes were a cold, indifferent aqua, reflecting the icy depths of his soul.

Darren was introverted and standoffish, preferring to keep to himself and avoid unnecessary interactions with others. He had a dominating presence that made people nervous around him, and he didn’t like his things touched or taken from him. He was very literal in his thinking, stubborn in his beliefs, and had a tendency to be possessive over the people he cared about.

Alice, on the other hand, was a stark contrast to Darren. Standing at a petite 5’5, she was a delicate beauty with an air of innocence about her. Her pure heart shone through her gentle demeanor, attracting those around her like moths to a flame. She had a kind and compassionate nature, always willing to lend a helping hand to those in need.

Despite their differences, Darren and Alice had a connection that ran deeper than words could describe. They had known each other since they were children, growing up in the same small town and forging a bond that nothing could break. Darren was fiercely protective of Alice, always watching over her like a guardian angel.
Darren towered over her, his dark hair spilling over his shoulders like a waterfall of shadow. His green eyes, usually so vibrant like emeralds, now glinted coldly, devoid of warmth. “You were meant to be mine,” he whispered, his voice a chilling blend of anger and longing. “A promise made, a promise broken. I will make you understand the weight of your father’s betrayal.”
Alice shivered, not from the cold of the castle but from the ice that had settled in Darren’s heart. Such beauty he possessed, yet it was marred by the darkness that seeped into every word he spoke. She knew of the stories whispered in the halls of her father’s court—tales of Darren’s malice, of the wicked deeds that had left scars on both his people and his soul.

“Why are you doing this?” She demanded, fury igniting within her chest as they entered his dimly lit study. “You think you can just take me?”
His lips twisted into a smirk that sent shivers down her spine. “I don’t just take what I want—I claim it.” He released her wrist but stepped closer, invading her space until she felt trapped against the wall.
Alice’s heart raced—not from fear alone but from an undeniable spark ignited between them. She hated him for what he represented: tyranny cloaked in charm and beauty. Yet there was something intoxicating about his presence—something that stirred forbidden desires within.

“Do you think your threats scare me?” she shot back defiantly even as heat pooled low in her belly at his proximity.
But beneath his icy exterior lay vulnerability—a man tormented by expectations and haunted by shadows cast from past mistakes. In moments when their gazes locked across the room's distance, Alice glimpsed something deeper than mere dominance; there was pain masked by arrogance.
The tension escalated until one fateful night broke them both open like fragile glass under pressure. A thunderstorm brewed outside; rain lashed against windows while lightning illuminated Darren’s face—sharp angles softened momentarily in flickering light.
“Why do you fight this?” he asked softly, stepping closer until there was barely any space left between them.
“I hate you,” she breathed out despite how much she wanted to lean into him—to feel warmth radiate off his body instead of cold stone walls surrounding them both.
His hand brushed against hers—a tentative touch that sent shockwaves through them both before he closed the distance entirely
